title: Design System: Abhishek Shukla, Data Analyst

display.purpose: The name on the instrument only; surname on its own line in 400 italic.

headline.purpose: Section heads, contact slip title, payee value.

title.purpose: Case study titles; registers use the face at 1.3rem and 1.15rem.

body.purpose: Running text with tabular numerals; 56ch intros, 68ch case prose.

label.purpose: Uppercase captions for values, table headers, case detail subheads. Never above a section heading.

data.purpose: Codes, tool codes, periods, figure cells.

serial.purpose: Case serials (1.35rem instrument, 1.6rem stub); amount figure at 1.5rem 500.

textures.name: security-tint
textures.value: repeating-linear-gradient(115deg, transparent 0 7px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--guilloche) 6%, transparent) 7px 8px), repeating-linear-gradient(65deg, transparent 0 11px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--bronze) 5%, transparent) 11px 12px)

textures.name: instrument-inner-frame
textures.purpose: Engraved double frame on the instrument.

textures.name: microprint
textures.value: Azeret Mono 5.5px, 0.08em tracking, guilloche ink at 85% opacity, aria-hidden
textures.purpose: Ornamental rule on the instrument top and in the footer.

textures.name: tint-field-canvas
textures.value: 0.5px wavy lines, 9px pitch, 16% alpha, every third strand bronze
textures.purpose: Canvas field behind the instrument and the contact slip.

textures.name: rosette-canvas
textures.value: 36 phase-shifted sine strands (every third bronze, 35% alpha) plus rings x 5 hypotrochoid copies (38%), 0.4px lines; lobes = first KPI clamped 3..14, rings = tool count
textures.purpose: Placeholder in missing certificates; the hollow variant (one frame ring per tool, alternating teal and bronze at 70%, inside the lace band) is the seal's no-WebGL fallback.

textures.name: wire-seal
textures.value: three.js LineSegments, lobed torus (R 1, tube 0.085), tilt -0.38 rad; lobes = first KPI clamped 3..14; lace strands = tool count in var(--guilloche) at var(--wire-lace) (0.5 day / 0.7 night); meridian hoops = lobes x 5 in var(--bronze) at var(--wire-hoop) (0.24 day / 0.34 night); canvas inset -14% around the 260px medallion (132px below 760px)
textures.purpose: The instrument's seal, framing the portrait; falls back to the hollow rosette-canvas without WebGL.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Case detail open (0.45s height and opacity) and dialog entry (0.3s).

motion.name: guilloche-draw
motion.value: 1400ms tint field, 1800ms rosette, 2200ms wire seal (draw range), cubic ease-out
motion.purpose: One-time draw-in on load; drawn still under reduced motion.

motion.name: header-rule
motion.purpose: Header gains its rule after 24px of scroll.

motion.name: wire-seal-idle
motion.value: 0.07 rad/s turn; pointer lean up to 0.06 rad (x) and 0.08 rad (y), eased at 0.04 per frame
motion.purpose: The seal's only continuing motion; paused off-screen and on hidden tabs, one still frame under reduced motion; low-power renderer, DPR capped at 2, three.js in its own chunk.

narrative.overview:
The page is printed on security paper. The opening screen is one wide bank instrument: an issuer block with the name engraved large, a serial and type at the top right, a live seal (a near face-on wireframe lace ring, drawn only in lines, framing a round portrait), a payee line that carries the lead case study, an amount box for the one validated figure, and a MICR code line along the foot. Everything below is the paperwork that backs the instrument: case studies as counterfoil documents with perforated stubs, and about, experience, skills and certificates as ruled registers and statements. The contact block is a remittance slip.

The material is pale green-grey tint stock crossed by two fine diagonal line fields, with deep blue-black intaglio ink. Ornament comes from the craft of security printing itself (guilloche line fields, rosettes, microprint rules, perforations, MICR symbols), never from effects. Density is that of a financial document: ruled rows, tabular numerals, and small uppercase field captions that label values the way a printed form does. The night variant prints the same plate in pale ink on dark stock; nothing is restyled, only re-inked.

The system refuses the portfolio-category default: no dark gradient hero, no glass cards, no stat tiles, no scattered decorative effects. Figures appear in ruled tables or the single amount box, never as giant numbers.
keyCharacteristics: Tint paper with two crossing hairline fields (115deg teal at 6%, 65deg bronze at 5%) on every surface.
One engraved roman display face, one institutional sans, one data mono for serials, codes and figures.
Hairline rules do all the structural work; corners are square or 2px.
One oxblood seal ink, filled only on the "Open case study" action.
Guilloche drawn from the project's own figures: canvas tint fields and rosettes drawn in once on load, and a wireframe lace-ring seal that draws in once and then turns slowly.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: Oxblood is filled on one control only: "Open case study". Every other button is an ink outline. Once a case is open, its button drops back to ink ("Close case study").

rules.name: The Security Ink Rule
rules.body: Teal and bronze are printing inks, not interface colours. They draw ornament (line fields, rosettes, the seal's lace ring, microprint, list markers) and never carry text, borders of controls, or state.

rules.name: The Figures Are Data Rule
rules.body: Every number that is a claim (figures, counts, serials, periods) is set in the mono, right-aligned in a ruled column, or in the single amount box. Numbers are never enlarged into display type.

rules.name: The Field Caption Rule
rules.body: Uppercase label type captions a value beside or below it, as on a printed form. It never sits above a section heading.

rules.name: The Kerned FinTech Rule
rules.body: Wherever "FinTech" is set in the display face, pull the T in by -0.07em; Old Standard TT leaves a gap between n and T.

rules.name: The Printed Plate Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Depth comes from paper tone and engraved double frames; the seal impression is the only shadow and belongs to the seal button alone.

dos: **Do** print every surface on tint stock with the two crossing hairline fields; keep raised documents on bright plate with a ruled border.
**Do** fill oxblood only on "Open case study"; every other action is an ink outline that fills with ink on hover.
**Do** set every claimed number in Azeret Mono inside a ruled column, the amount box or a serial.

**Do** draw guilloche from real figures (lobes per KPI, rings per tool) and print its legend; draw it in once with a cubic ease-out (1.4s tint fields, 1.8s rosettes, 2.2s wire seal). Only the seal keeps moving, slowly, and everything renders still under reduced motion.
**Do** use dashed rules and perforations for tear lines between a stub and its document.
**Do** keep corners square on documents and 2px on controls.
**Do** keep the night variant a re-inking of the same plate: swap tokens, never layouts.
donts: **Don't** add a dark gradient hero, glass cards, stat tiles or decorative effects outside the security-printing vocabulary.
**Don't** use teal or bronze for text, control borders or state.
**Don't** add shadows to panels, cards or chips; the seal impression belongs to the seal button only.
**Don't** fake an image: missing screenshots and certificates show a labelled pending slip.
